newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy economy set to grow 0.5 pct in Q2 - Isco.
newsitem.headline: Italy economy set to grow 0.5 pct in Q2 - Isco.

text.p: The Italian economy should return to growth in the second quarter of 1997 after contracting in the first three months, due to more working days, economic research institute Isco said.

Gross domestic product (GDP) should grow 0.5 percent quarter on quarter in the April-June period, compared with the preliminary quarter on quarter fall of 0.3 percent in January-March, the state-funded institute forecast.

Isco economist Giovanni Palmerio told the budget commission of Italy's Senate or upper house of parliament the contraction in the first three months of the year was due to fewer working days than normal in the period.
"The opposite effect should support growth in the second quarter, most likely taking it above 0.5 percent," he said.
He said figures furnished by business in the institute's latest economic survey confirmed the possibility of consolidation of a recovery in production this spring.

According to national statistics institute Istat GDP contracted 0.5 percent year on year in the first quarter, compared with expansion of 0.1 percent year on year in the fourth quarter of 1996 and contraction of 0.2 percent quarter on quarter in the same period.
Palmerio said Isco's forecast for Italian inflation this year was an average 2.1 percent, lower than the government's forecast of 2.5 percent.
He said the 1998 forecast was for prices growth of 2.0 percent. The government's forecast is 1.8 percent in 1998.
